newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech SPT sees dividends after investment.
newsitem.headline: Czech SPT sees dividends after investment.

text.p: The chairman of the Czech fixed-line monopoly SPT Telecom a.s. said on Friday that dividends would only be paid in the foreseeable future if profits exceed the need for investment.
"At this moment we are not deciding on future dividends," Lubos Rezabek told a news conference after the company's annual general meeting.

"(The board of directors) will recommended dividend payments in the future years only in the case that we are sure that we have covered the financial demands of our investment and still have some free (funds remaining)," he said.

SPT's long-term modernisation plan, which covers the years 1996 to 2002, has called for 130-150 billion crowns to be invested, equalling average investment of roughly 30 billion crowns each year during the period.
SPT posted a 483 million crown 1996 net loss as the company made one-off provisions against structural changes after a 4.83 billion crown net profit for 1995.
The firm posted the loss, according to international accounting standards (IAS), due to one-time extraordinary charges of 8.757 billion crowns.
About 1.75 billion crowns of this was taken as the firm prepares for layoffs and restructuring that should see SPT shed some 10,000 of its current 26,800 workforce by the year 2000.
Shareholders approved on Friday the board's proposal for a 10-for-1 stock split. The move still must be processed through the Prague Stock Exchange and it is not yet clear when it would be executed.
